en: He assembled a host of many falcons,
After he issued this command,
Folding his arms and cutting off heads,
God struck down his army,
The beast arose and showed its valor.
A cloud of majesty arose,
The rear-guard champion Jooshuk,
His strength was famed among the host,
Then the warrior crouched low,
A champion emerged among a thousand,
Known among every people,
All the Kyrgyz fell into uproar,
They leveled their spears firmly,
The earth split in that hour,
Every tethered horse stood ready,
Dust rose so thick the eye could not see,
If you saw it, smoke and flame filled the conflict,
The Kyrgyz stood alone, a gathered host,
The measured ground could not contain them,
Their spears could not reach their limit,
The dear Kyrgyz, a mighty army,
The day boiled with the massed foe,
A thousand Chinese against one Kyrgyz,
When he struck, he dragged them aside,
He scattered blood across the great host,
A single soul remained alive,
They swarmed like ants,
The earth turned slick beneath the trampling,
Chinese troops attacked from every side,
They came back from ages past,
The foe died and the feud remained,
Wrath stretched long,
The enemy remained upon the dear earth,
When the Chinese engulfed them,
In a brief stormy moment,
When distress descended upon their heads,
Calling it grief that came from China,
At the place where they clashed,
The warriors stood firm-kneed,
They never took their eyes from the hero,
Upon the head of the one who emerged,
They honored his glory.
The warrior Odukan appeared immense,
He hastened with immeasurable strength,
He had burning fury and flame,
An enemy life was fixed in his thoughts,
His rising rage scorched living souls,
Now it was Ebegey above all,
They prayed he might find a stratagem,
Saying that death is kin to every mortal,
One who could restore a life nearly severed,
When they hewed at one another squarely,
He could scatter four thousand at the pass,
They said the warrior was left like an old man,
Toward the Kerik standing ready,
They mounted Zhelzhetpes upon it,
Rousing his spirit and setting him upright,
His death-defying comrades stood with him,
Showing the victory of a hero,
He fell into hands filled with misfortune,
The warrior Zhelzhetpes burned with anguish,
From among the multitude of warriors,
A swelling conflict began,
Kögöy’s precious life hung by a thread,
Kenen entrusted the fallen one to them,
His life, tiny as a fly, grew faint,
His eyes burned as he faced the true world beyond,
The wrathful enemy formation was broken,
The great and numerous Kyrgyz people,
Precious Kenen and Ebegey,
The four stood and greeted one another,
Infidel and Muslim alike,
Do not forget the turmoil if you seek it,
Rage stirred up the rebellion,
They waged a fierce conflict,
Mounted on Kerik, he raced through the dust,
Taking the road toward safety,
He escaped out of the turmoil.
From the thunder with which he entered,
From the furious Chinese host,
A rare one who became a lion,
Burning with difficulty,
Seeing it, he gave his word,
Today my father summons me,
He stood while the day settled,
Behind you was a day of peace,
He was a son who knew the prayer,
To China he was red poison,
To the Kyrgyz he was their destined banner,
When he struck the foe amid the dust,
May God grant him to the Kyrgyz,
The ravine split and the cliff collapsed,
He laid waste the broad land,
Making his battle spirit known,
Their arms thrashed as they met,
Clouds covered the mountain,
Across low ridges and open plain,
They surged apart in wrath,
As though digging lightning from the sky,
Spurring horses, the seal fell,
Finish them; do not fear,
I shall crush and drag them away,
He aligned the stones and pressed in,
Every living creature,
Grew still and then trembled,
Thunder spread far and wide,
From fighting he could no longer see,
The people’s lament knotted within,
Every creature that came to mind,
Appeared while still alive,
The creatures upon the earth,
The ember in their breasts tightened,
He drove the foe straight through,
Across the drifting haze and cliffs.
Taking a bare, round stone,
With a bent rope twisted back,
Taking hide and piling it layer upon layer,
He arranged it broad and smooth as a saddle-cloth.
He bound the hands so eyes would reel,
He barred every visible road.
No living soul could pass through the breastwork,
No living soul could pass the spell-worker.
Thus he blew his incantation,
Leaving no way to turn back.
He set its course straight,
For the harsh doom that pursued him,
He set its right path straight.
For the hardship spread in secret,
He set its snare straight.
When he looked all around,
Hoping for the safety of the people,
He failed to meet those he should meet,
And met those who should never be met.
In the time it took him to close his eyes,
An untimely death overtook him.
He was struck down by a dagger,
And their spears were set against him.
The iron rope tightened,
He fell into the net, alas.
Its kick was beyond a man’s power to cut,
He fell into misery, alas.
Wherever he went, grim death would not relent,
He fell into their hands, alas.

Road to death was made ready.
The wrestlers’ equipment was prepared.
When they fought, none came near his measure.
Examine the superior wrestler;
Set the spears for the contest.
Countless wrestlers gathered together.
His true stratagem lay amid the multitude,
He threaded through them swift as wind,
Reaching the ground, he wounded them,
His eyes wandered in alarm,
His legs dragged loose beneath him,
His tormented soul cried out,
All withered and groaned,
They became one mass of blood,
Both hands labored in battle,
They vanished like scattered livestock,
Dear youth, for whom standing was difficult,
His eyes became bowls of blood,
His chest grew constricted,
Unable to stand upright,
One mighty man fell,
The youth collapsed without bending back,
He despaired of life,
The cold, terrible bullet of death,
The shot was heard beyond the mountain,
His true soul cried aloud,
His whole body failed,
He crumbled like ground millet,
Ebegey fell into their hands,
He turned and drew back,
Ebegey took to the road,
Unable to break through the front,
Ebegey fell into the snare,
Entering the skirmish, he scattered them,
His ribs piled up beneath the bruising,
One side of his lungs was crushed,
His insides heaved toward the great grave,
From father and mother came Jooluk,
A great cloud cast into the massed battle,
Saying the grave he was given was fitting,
The men of Beijing approved the ruin,
The untrenched camp watched with open eyes.
Saying, “Let that young ram be hung,”
After he had gone into their midst,
They struck him with an axe, calling him a hero.
They drove him against stone and crag.
At the end of the world,
Thinking, “I can strive onward and reach it,”
If he paid no heed to the Kalmyks,
So that even the aged would know,
The dark maral’s antlers branched apart,
For those who walked upon the earth,
For those who would possess the whole world,
Against immeasurable giants,
Against the multitude, old and full-grown,
Against the man who resisted,
His heart was young and treated the deed lightly.
When you see him, he is terrible to an enemy.
He threw the great host into turmoil,
Thinking, “I shall lay them down before his eyes.”
Against that one who would not obey,
Against the silent one who submitted,
Against the watchful, complete host,
Against the hero who resisted,
He made them endure true hardship,
And sent a rain of bullets over them.
He had them shot by Chengker,
Thus he settled their account.
Of the one who kept resisting,
He would dig out the dark spirit.
If an enemy rose within a handspan,
He plunged him into black blood.
If he was a hero who crossed the pass,
If he was a champion who grappled belt to belt,
He had him shot down again,
And made him taste close combat.
Blood by day, blood by night—
When he stood passing through wrath,
The marksman Chengker saw him.
Saying, “Give me your ribs,”
Saying, “I truly passed straight through,”
No flame could pierce the foe they found,
Though one bullet passed, another would not,
Kondoy, armored to the mouth,
The courage of Kanday,
Saying he himself had passed straight through,
Ebegey, renowned in song,
Saying it was the time he stood there,
The marksman’s cast,
Parting from the world,
A half-blackened mass,
At that very moment of his soul,

Is poor man still alive?
From death and torment,
By the command of the one who burst forth,
Astonished, yet not grieving,
Untiring before the scythe-like edge,
Roaming until his strength bled away,
The milk-white horse beneath him,

Ebegey of those three days,
